clue.text: Deprived worker perhaps judged in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means we go by how the preceding words sound when spoken, not how they are spelt

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
to ref is to referee, so judged a match

explanation.surface: A worker deprived of something has their case judged at a tribunal hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'bee reffed' quickly and it runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft describes someone robbed or left lacking, so it matches the adjective sense of deprived.

clue.text: Experts capturing fifty frauds

indicators.note: capturing means the first word's letters hold the next item inside them like a prisoner

parts.note: buffs are enthusiasts who know a subject well
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Specialists catch fifty people running scams.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluffs are deceptions or pretences, so the plural noun matches frauds in the sense of tricks.

clue.text: The man's novel with such rewrites might make Christmas present

indicators.note: novel means new, so the combined letters appear in a fresh arrangement
with such says the answer joins the first words to make the phrase that follows, so the answer is that phrase less those words

parts.note: the target phrase, taken as written
taken as written, letters to be taken away from the target phrase

explanation.surface: Someone rewriting a novel imagines it could become a Christmas present.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: THE MAN'S plus the answer's letters rearrange into CHRISTMAS PRESENT, so take THE MAN'S out and shuffle what is left into RESCRIPTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescript is a rewriting of something, so rescripts is a plural noun meaning versions written again.

clue.text: Rows around lake and escapes

indicators.note: around means the first word's letters go about the next item, enclosing it

parts.note: rows, rhyming with cows, are quarrels
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Arguments around a lake lead to people running away.
explanation.walkthrough: Rows here are noisy quarrels, not lines of seats or boat trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight means fleeing, so flights are acts of running away from danger or capture.

clue.text: Coin stuck in meter provoked anger

indicators.note: stuck in means one item is lodged inside the other
provoked suggests something stirred up, so the letters of meter are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a bit is an old name for a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A coin jammed in a parking meter made the driver furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provoked anger' reads as one phrase, but provoked works on meter and anger alone is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter is to make someone resentful, which is close to the verb sense of anger: to enrage.

clue.text: Man who presented half hour following dull politician

indicators.note: following means the first piece named comes after the one named later

parts.note: matt describes a dull, non-shiny finish
Tony Hancock starred in the British radio and TV comedy Hancock's Half Hour

explanation.surface: A dull politician follows a man who once hosted a half-hour show.
explanation.walkthrough: Hancock's Half Hour was a famous 1950s British sitcom; Matt Hancock is a British Conservative former health secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Matt Hancock was a Conservative MP and cabinet minister, so he is an example of a politician.

clue.text: Set up home close to Boris? Unlikely

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: close to means the closing letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of the name
a tall story is an unlikely one

explanation.surface: Someone sets up home next door to Boris Johnson, which seems improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to Boris' looks like nearness to a person but takes his name's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To install something is to put it in place ready for use, the verb sense of set up.

clue.text: Thinking not fluid matter

indicators.note: not means the next item is excluded from the first word

parts.note: taken as written
ink is a writing fluid

explanation.surface: Rigid thinking doesn't count for much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' seems to describe the thinking; it is a noun, the ink removed from the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is an object or affair, as in 'what's the matter?', so both nouns name some unspecified business.

clue.text: Soldiers overturned senior with a gun

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the following string is flipped end to end

parts.note: Sr is the abbreviation for senior
taken as written
a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: Troops capsized a senior officer who was armed with a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulars are professional full-time troops of a standing army, as opposed to reservists.

clue.text: Silent assistance by local individuals

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so one piece sits next to the other

parts.note: 'uns is dialect for ones, as in young 'uns
aid is help

explanation.surface: Neighbours give help without saying a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' signals dialect: 'uns is a regional form of 'ones'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsaid is left unspoken, so the adjective matches silent in the sense of not voiced.

clue.text: Hiding pain when husband parts

indicators.note: parts means splits open, so the first word is divided to admit others

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Hiding the hurt when a husband leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' reads as departs; it is a verb meaning splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Stashing means storing away out of sight, the same as hiding something in a secret place.

clue.text: River breadth striking daughter immediately

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river

indicators.note: striking here means striking out, crossing off the next item

parts.note: width is breadth
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A river's breadth hits a daughter at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like hitting; it is striking out the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthwith is a formal adverb meaning without delay, at once.

clue.text: Stupidly, inspector of ear advanced inside sick Yankee

indicators.note: inside means the preceding items are placed within the following ones

parts.note: ill means sick
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
DI is Detective Inspector
otic is the adjective relating to the ear
A is the abbreviation for advanced

explanation.surface: A police inspector foolishly examines an ear inside a sick American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspector of ear' looks like an ear doctor, but it splits into the detective and the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotically means in a foolish manner, an adverb like stupidly.

clue.text: Guardian article on reflecting

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: reflecting means mirrored, so the word for on is read backwards

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Guardian suggests the newspaper. Cricket's on side and leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel watches over a person, so angel names a protective spirit.

clue.text: Kick the bucket holding one fine and humble plant

indicators.note: holding means the phrase before it keeps the next item within it

parts.note: to kick the bucket is to die, or pass on
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
to humble someone is to lower them

explanation.surface: Someone dies clutching a single delicate, lowly plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The passionflower is a climbing vine with distinctive flowers, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Revolutionary act getting you nowhere?

parts.note: surface reading: an uprising or radical deed that achieves nothing
setter's reading: a turning motion of tyres on a car that spins in place without moving forward

explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary suggests politics, but here it means rotating.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheelspin is when a vehicle's driven tyres turn without grip, so the car goes nowhere.

clue.text: Assassin with half-hearted deed that's dropped

indicators.note: half-hearted means losing half of the heart, one of the two central letters

parts.note: Casca was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar
taken as written

explanation.surface: An assassin carries out a half-hearted killing that gets abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of a four-letter word is its middle two letters; half of that is one E.
explanation.definitionFit: To cascade is to fall in a stream, so cascaded is a past tense matching dropped as fell.

clue.text: A mineral unrefined reportedly way used to increase fitness

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the words count for their sound

parts.note: salt is a mineral
coarse means crude or unrefined

explanation.surface: Crude salt is apparently being used in a new keep-fit regime.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault course is an obstacle route for military or fitness training, and course gives the route sense.

clue.text: One speaking is plain about upset

parts.note: utter means downright, as in plain or utter nonsense

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A speaker is obviously distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak, so an utterer is a person who voices words.

clue.text: Flier penned by band's writer

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed as in a pen, so the first item sits inside the next

parts.note: a ring is a circular band
an owl is a bird, something that flies

explanation.surface: A pilot is mentioned in a songwriter's lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' hints at writing, but it means shut in.
explanation.definitionFit: J. K. Rowling is the author of the Harry Potter novels, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Prose about unknown winged beast

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
algebra uses x, y and z as unknowns

explanation.surface: Writing about a mysterious flying creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey, so it is a creature with wings.

clue.text: One helping Santa arrive before time

indicators.note: before means the first piece is placed ahead of the next

parts.note: come means arrive
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An elf assisting Father Christmas turns up before the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: Comet is one of Santa's reindeer in 'A Visit from St Nicholas', who pull his sleigh.

clue.text: Told places where Americans buy mangles

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the following phrase counts by its sound

parts.note: shopping malls are American shopping centres

explanation.surface: Someone is told where Americans go to buy laundry wringers.
explanation.walkthrough: A mangle is also an old wringer for laundry, so 'buy mangles' reads as one shopping trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To maul is to savage or tear something, so mauls is a verb matching mangles in the sense of damages.

clue.text: Weak slack oddball gets easy tasks

indicators.note: an oddball is eccentric, so the letters behave oddly and come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A feeble, lazy eccentric is given undemanding jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cakewalk is an informal word for something very easy to do, so cakewalks are simple jobs.

clue.text: Funny taking in odd sound from instrument

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so the first word holds the next one

parts.note: droll means amusing in a dry way
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An amusing noise comes from an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumroll is a rapid series of beats played on a drum, a sound produced by an instrument.

clue.text: Exchanging tips with muscular diver

indicators.note: exchanging tips means the first and last letters swap places

parts.note: ripped is slang for very muscular

explanation.surface: Trading advice with a muscle-bound diver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like advice; it means the ends of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The dipper is a small bird that dives and walks underwater in streams to feed.

clue.text: Ruins of French settlements vacated outside city of Paris

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: outside means those letters go around the following item
vacated means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
Paris was a prince of Troy in Greek myth

explanation.surface: French ruins of abandoned villages lie on the edge of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City of Paris' is not the French capital but the Trojan prince's home.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy is to wreck, so destroys is a present-tense verb matching ruins.

clue.text: Business of mature couple's opening in New York

parts.note: to age is to mature

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside what follows

parts.note: NY is the standard abbreviation for New York

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the first letter of couple

explanation.surface: An older couple start a company in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a firm providing a service, such as a travel agency, so it is a type of business.
